subject: Clarify pricing: tool/system token split & rounding for committed discount
messages:
From: Jessica Lam <jessica.lam@acme-ai.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-28T09:17:00-07:00
Subject: Questions on 'rate card' — tool tokens, system tokens, and rounding

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for sharing the draft rate card earlier. A few follow-ups from our engineering and finance teams before we run internal numbers:

1) When you say 'tokens billed = input + output + system + tool', how exactly are system and tool tokens counted? For example: if we include a 50-token system prompt per session and call an external tool that returns 120 tokens in its response, are those 120 tool tokens added to the same request and rounded together, or billed as a separate call?

2) Rounding: we saw a note about rounding at the request level. How does that behave for streaming responses (where tokens arrive in chunks) and for function/tool calls (tool may stream back partial payloads)? We want to avoid a scenario where many tiny chunks blow up our bill due to per-chunk rounding.

3) Discount application: if we hit a committed monthly spend, is the discount applied to 'billed tokens' after rounding? Or to raw counts before rounding?

I've attached a tiny sample of our typical traffic (acme-usage-sample.csv) and a simple scenario where we estimate 120M gen tokens/month. If you could provide numeric examples and an effective $/1M-tokens after the discount, that would be super helpful for procurement.

Best,
Jessica Lam
Head of Infrastructure
Acme AI

Attachment: acme-usage-sample.csv (CSV stub, 12 rows)

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on 'rate card' — tool tokens, system tokens, and rounding

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear examples and the sample CSV. Looping in Karthik (SE) and Marissa (pricing) to get precise math and options. High level answers below so you can share with procurement while we finalize the numbers: 

- Billing unit: hosted API bills by tokens consumed by the request/response lifecycle. That includes: model input tokens (prompt + system messages), model output tokens (generation), and any tool-call output tokens produced by the model invoking a tool (we treat tool-call output as part of the end-to-end call unless the tool is a separate API call).

- Rounding: default policy is 'round up to the nearest whole token at the final RPC boundary' — i.e., we do not round per streaming chunk, we round on request completion. For function/tool calls that are performed as distinct RPCs in our API, each RPC will be rounded separately. Practically: a streaming generation that produces 123.4 tokens will be billed as 124 tokens for that request. If the request includes one or more internal system messages (e.g., 50 tokens) those are added to the same RPC's total before rounding.

- Discount application: discounts are applied to the billed spend after rounding and aggregation. For standard hosted commitments, we aggregate usage daily and apply discounts on the invoiced amount (post-rounding). If you need a different arrangement (e.g., pre-rounding discounting or custom metering), that is possible under a negotiated contract and we can scope it into the SLA.

I attached the current ratecard (Redwood_Ratecard_v2.xlsx) and we'll follow up with worked examples. Karthik — can you add 2 numeric examples (streaming + function call) showing how we count and how the discount would affect $/1M tokens?

Thanks,
Hannah Schmitt
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on 'rate card' — tool tokens, system tokens, and rounding

Hi Jessica — quick concrete examples below (numbers simplified for clarity). Quoting Hannah's summary above.

Example A — single streaming generation (one RPC)
- system messages: 50 tokens (sent with the request)
- user prompt: 150 tokens
- model streams back 732.6 tokens total (arrives as several chunks)
Billing: (50 + 150 + 732.6) = 932.6 -> rounded up at RPC end -> 933 billed tokens for that call.

Example B — model calls a tool, tool returns text (tool implemented as separate RPC)
- initial request (RPC #1): system 30 + prompt 80 -> model decides to call tool (no output tokens billed for RPC #1 other than decision tokens; we bill actual tokens consumed) -> round as usual for RPC #1
- tool call (RPC #2): external tool returns 120 tokens (this is a distinct RPC that we bill as tool-output tokens); tool-output is billed as part of the customer's usage. If the tool's output is stitched into a subsequent model RPC (RPC #3) that final RPC's tokens are billed separately.

So in a tool flow where tool output is returned as a separate RPC, you get multiple rounded boundaries (RPC #2 rounded independently). That said, we do not round per stream chunk inside an RPC; only at RPC completion, which avoids blow-ups from many small stream frames.

Discount math (example): base list price = $4.00 / 1M tokens (generation lines). If Acme commits to $50k/month we can offer 10% off list; $150k/month unlocks 20% off.

- Base: $4.00 / 1M -> for your 120M estimate = $480.00 (list)
- 10% off -> $3.60 / 1M -> 120M = $432.00
- 20% off -> $3.20 / 1M -> 120M = $384.00

Note: these numbers are illustrative; Marissa will provide final price bands and confirm whether tool tokens are eligible for the discount in standard terms (they are by default). If you want to exclude a specific 'partner tool' or third-party vendor's tokens from the discount, we can carve that out in contract but it requires explicit scoping.

Attachment: worked_examples.pdf (stub) — I included the step-by-step token tables.

—Karthik
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Questions on 'rate card' — tool tokens, system tokens, and rounding

Hi Jessica — thanks for the clear asks. Finalized numbers and contract options below: 

1) Effective rates (post-rounding, aggregated daily) — we express per 1M tokens for simplicity: 
- List: $4.00 / 1M tokens
- 10% commit (>= $50k/mo): $3.60 / 1M tokens (effective, after daily aggregation & rounding)
- 20% commit (>= $150k/mo): $3.20 / 1M tokens

Effective examples you requested (post-discount)
- 120M tokens @ 20% -> 120 * $3.20 = $384.00
- 1B tokens @ 20% -> 1000 * $3.20 = $3,200.00

Note on the 'exclude a tool' request: we can support a contract carve-out. Implementation options: 
A) Contractual carve-out: we mark the named tool as 'excluded' in the SOW; token usage attributed to that tool (identified by the tool_id in your requests) will be billed at list price and will not be reduced by the committed discount. Billing will still reflect rounded counts but discount is applied only to the non-excluded usage.
B) Metering rule (technical): we can add a tag to the RPC (e.g., x-client-tool-id) and our billing pipeline will keep that usage as a separate line item. This requires an engineering change (small) and contract amendment.

Example with carve-out (120M baseline, tool invoked 30% of sessions, tool-output accounts for ~18M tokens):
- Total billed tokens pre-exclude: 120M -> base cost @ list = 120 * $4.00 = $480.00
- Excluded tool tokens (18M) billed at list = 18 * $4.00 = $72.00
- Remaining 102M at 20% discounted rate = 102 * $3.20 = $326.40
- Invoice total = $72.00 + $326.40 = $398.40 -> effective blended rate = $398.40 / 120 = $3.32 / 1M tokens

Operational notes: the billing granularity will be daily lines (excluded vs discounted). Rounding is still per RPC; aggregation applies before discounting.

If that blended math works for you, we can draft a SOW with the excluded-tool clause and a HubSpot deal addendum. For the 20% band we require a 12-month minimum commitment (monthly invoiced, pre-pay optional). Once you confirm, I'll prepare the SOW and DocuSign.

Regards,

Head of Pricing, Redwood Inference
